question: Will Dan Koh be the Democratic nominee for MA-06?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the MA-06 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on September 15, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

evidence.excerpt: Compiled for the North Shore/Merrimack Valley news consortium. Massachusetts’ 6th Congressional District primary is September 1, 2026; the general election is November 3, 2026. Rep. Seth Moulton is not seeking re-election to the seat he’s held since 2015; he’s running in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate against Sen. Ed Markey.

evidence.publisher: Dan Koh for Congress — campaign press release
evidence.excerpt: Today, Dan Koh’s campaign launched a new ad, “Democrats You Trust,” featuring President Biden, Vice President Harris, the Massachusetts AFL-CIO, and local Democratic leaders who have endorsed his campaign for Congress. The new advertising follows a newly released poll that shows Dan with a 19 point lead in the field, building on months of on-the-ground organizing, more than 100 endorsements from labor organizations, elected officials, and community leaders, and a record fundraising operation that has out-paced every other candidate in the race.

According to the campaign, the survey of 400 likely Democratic primary voters was conducted by Global Strategy Group between July 30 and Aug. 2 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.9 percentage points. The poll found Koh with 34% support, followed by Beccia at 15% and Nguyen at 14%. Twenty-four percent of respondents were undecided. Campaign-commissioned polls are common during election campaigns and should not be considered independent surveys.

According to Federal Election Commission filings covering activity through June 30, Koh reported about $3 million cash on hand, the largest campaign treasury in the race. Beccia followed with roughly $2.3 million, much of it from personal loans to his campaign. State Rep. Tram Nguyen, who represents Andover, North Andover, Boxford and part of Tewksbury, reported several hundred thousand dollars available, while Jamie Belsito, Mariah Lancaster and Bethany Andres-Beck each reported substantially smaller cash reserves.

Beth Andres-Beck, John Beccia, Dan Koh, Mariah Lancaster, Tram Nguyen, and Jamie Zahlaway Belsito are running in the Democratic primary for Massachusetts' 6th Congressional District on Sept. 1. Incumbent Seth Moulton (D) is running for the U.S. Senate to represent Massachusetts. The election is set against the backdrop of affordability and opposing President Donald Trump's (R) administration.

Koh’s campaign said it raised more than $1 million between April and June, bringing its fundraising total to more than $4.5 million since launching the campaign. Nguyen, an Andover Democrat who represents the 18th Essex District in the Massachusetts House, announced Thursday that she raised $266,000 during the second quarter — the largest quarterly total of her campaign. According to her campaign, Nguyen has now raised more than $690,000 since entering the race from 2,827 individual donors.

The poll, commissioned by Nguyen’s campaign and conducted May 26-27 by Workbench Strategy, found Nguyen leading the six-candidate field with 28% support among likely Democratic primary voters. Former Biden administration official Dan Koh was second at 18%, while 24% of respondents remained undecided. The Workbench poll surveyed 400 likely Democratic primary voters and has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.89 percentage points. Interviews were conducted through a combination of live telephone calls and text invitations to an online survey.

Massachusetts is holding U.S. House primaries on Sept. 1, 2026. In Massachusetts, the winner of a primary election is the candidate who receives the greatest number of votes, even if the candidate does not receive an outright majority of votes cast.
